$comment: The wire contract for who the voice gate heard (M71).
`speaker-end` already reaches the client that ran the turn. This event
is for everything else watching the house — the console's activity
strip and the phone's — which otherwise had no way to draw 'a stranger
spoke to the kitchen satellite'. Three readers hold to it: jarvis-core's
tests/test_speaker_gate.py asserts the pipeline fires exactly these
android-app/tools/activity_mirror_test.py hold the two strips to the row
rule below. A shared table rather than a comment saying 'keep in step',
because a comment has never once kept anything in step.
`label` is WHO, and it is set only when the gate accepted the voice; a
refusal carries `label: null` and names the closest enrolled person in
`nearest`, so a consumer that reads 'label: Ted' as 'Ted spoke' is never
handed the nearest miss under the same key. `reason` is the verifier's
own word; the ones in `unverifiable_reasons` mean 'could not judge' —
too short, no pitch — and a strip must not paint those as a stranger.
No event ever carries audio, a vector, or the transcript. The voiceprint
never leaves the server, and the bus is not the place to start.
